items: Round trip US East <-> US West
All values approximate, order-of-magnitude; hardware varies by generation and cloud.

drills.title: Average QPS from DAU
drills.prompt:
A social app has **50 million DAU**. Each user makes on average **20 API requests per day**.

What is the **average** request rate?
drills.takeaway: ~12k req/s average is a modest fleet of stateless servers; the hard part is the peak and the data tier.

drills.title: Peak QPS with diurnal skew
drills.prompt:
An internal Microsoft Teams-style presence service sees **200 million requests/day**. Traffic is concentrated: plan for a **peak-to-average ratio of 3x**.

What peak request rate should you provision for?
drills.takeaway: Provision for peak (plus headroom), not average, or the morning login wave will tip you over.

drills.title: Payments API peak at Black Friday
drills.prompt:
A payments processor handles **500 million charges per year**. On Black Friday, volume is **8x the average day**, and within that day the busiest hour carries **10% of the day's charges**. Each charge results in **5 internal API calls**.

What is the peak internal API call rate during that busiest hour?
assumptions: 10% of daily volume in peak hour
drills.takeaway: Fan-out multiplies external load; size internal services on calls, not charges.

drills.title: Storage for short posts over 5 years
drills.prompt:
A microblogging service gets **100 million new posts/day**. Each post stores **300 bytes of text + 200 bytes metadata**. Data is kept **5 years** and **replicated 3x**.

How much total storage is needed (TB)?
drills.takeaway: Text is cheap: a few hundred TB fits a modest sharded cluster; media will dominate.

drills.title: Photo storage with replication
drills.prompt:
A photo-sharing app gets **2 million photo uploads/day**, average **2 MB** each. Three thumbnails add **10%** extra. Photos are kept **forever**; plan **3 years**. Object storage uses **erasure coding with 1.5x overhead**.

How much raw storage is needed after 3 years (PB)?
drills.takeaway: Erasure coding halves the bill versus triple replication at PB scale.

drills.title: Ledger storage at a payments company
drills.prompt:
Every charge writes **4 ledger entries** (double-entry, auth + capture) of **250 bytes** each, plus **1 KB** of indexes per charge. Volume: **1 billion charges/year**. Retain **7 years** for compliance, **3 replicas**.

Total storage (TB)?
drills.takeaway: Financial ledgers are small in bytes; correctness and auditability, not capacity, drive the design.

drills.title: Document DB working set
drills.prompt:
A MongoDB collection holds **400 million documents**, average **1.5 KB**. Indexes add **25%** of data size. The **hot 20%** of documents plus **all indexes** should fit in the WiredTiger cache.

How much RAM is needed for the working set (GB)?
drills.takeaway: Indexes often dominate the working set; trim unused indexes before buying RAM.

drills.title: Shards needed for a document store
drills.prompt:
Total dataset is **12 TB** (after compression) and grows **50%** over the planning horizon. Each shard (replica set) should hold at most **2 TB** to keep backups and initial sync fast.

How many shards?
steps: Answer: 9 shards (each a 3-node replica set = 27 nodes)
assumptions: Even distribution via a good shard key
drills.takeaway: Shard count is often set by operational limits (resync time), not raw disk.

drills.title: Shards from write throughput
drills.prompt:
An IoT platform ingests **2 million sensor readings/s at peak**, batched into inserts. Each replica-set primary can sustain **60k inserts/s** at **70%** target utilisation of that number.

How many shards are needed?
drills.takeaway: Write-bound workloads scale by shards; a hashed or bucketed shard key avoids a hot primary.

drills.title: Video streaming egress
drills.prompt:
A streaming service has **2 million concurrent viewers** at peak, average bitrate **4 Mbps**.

What is the peak egress bandwidth (Tbps)?
assumptions: All traffic served from CDN edge
drills.takeaway: Multi-Tbps egress is a CDN problem; origin must only handle cache misses.

drills.title: Upload bandwidth for photos
drills.prompt:
Users upload **5 million photos/day** at **3 MB** each. Peak is **3x** average.

What is peak ingress bandwidth (Gbps)?
drills.takeaway: A handful of 10G NICs handle ingress; storage write throughput is the real constraint.

drills.title: Video conferencing bandwidth per SFU
drills.prompt:
A Teams-style SFU hosts meetings of **10 participants**. Each sends one **1.5 Mbps** stream; the SFU forwards every stream to the **other 9**. A server has a **10 Gbps NIC**, planned at **60%** utilisation.

How many concurrent meetings can one SFU host (bandwidth-bound)?
drills.takeaway: Egress grows O(n^2) with meeting size; simulcast and active-speaker limits are essential.

drills.title: Web servers needed
drills.prompt:
Peak traffic is **60,000 req/s**. Each app server handles **2,000 req/s** at target CPU. You want **N+30%** headroom for failures and deploys.

How many servers?
drills.takeaway: Server counts are cheap to compute; the headroom policy is the interesting design decision.

drills.title: Servers from latency and concurrency
drills.prompt:
A fraud-scoring service receives **8,000 req/s** at peak. Each request takes **50 ms** of wall time but only **10 ms CPU**. Each server has **16 cores** and runs **200 concurrent request slots** (async I/O). Target **60%** CPU.

How many servers are needed (take the larger of CPU-bound and concurrency-bound)?
steps: Concurrency (Little's law): 8,000 x 0.05 s = 400 in flight
drills.takeaway: Little's law plus CPU-seconds tells you which resource actually binds.

drills.title: Redis cache for hot keys
drills.prompt:
A product catalog has **50 million items**, each cached value **5 KB**. **20%** of items get 80% of traffic. Redis overhead is **~1.3x** of raw value size.

How much memory to cache the hot set (GB)?
drills.takeaway: 65 GB fits a small Redis cluster (e.g. 3 shards x ~32 GB) with replicas.

drills.title: Session store memory
drills.prompt:
An Azure-hosted portal has **30 million concurrent sessions** at peak, each **2 KB**. Replicated **2x**.

Total memory (GB)?
drills.takeaway: Sessions fit comfortably in a distributed cache; keep them out of the primary DB.

drills.title: Kafka partitions for throughput
drills.prompt:
An event pipeline produces **500 MB/s** at peak. You plan **10 MB/s per partition** for producers, but each consumer instance can only process **5 MB/s**.

How many partitions does the topic need?
assumptions: Consumers scale only up to partition count
drills.takeaway: Partition count is usually set by consumer parallelism, and is hard to change later, so over-provision.

drills.title: Kafka broker disk for retention
drills.prompt:
A topic receives **200 MB/s** average, with **replication factor 3** and **7-day retention**.

Total cluster disk needed (TB)?
drills.takeaway: Retention x RF dominates; tiered storage or shorter retention is the main lever.

drills.title: Payment events to Kafka partitions
drills.prompt:
Peak payment events: **40,000 events/s**, each **2 KB**. Each partition is planned for **5 MB/s** and consumers handle **2,000 events/s** each.

Partitions needed?
steps: Max = 20 partitions (round up to e.g. 24-32 for growth)
drills.takeaway: Per-merchant ordering via keyed partitions works if no single merchant dominates.

drills.title: LSM write amplification
drills.prompt:
A storage engine using leveled compaction ingests **100 MB/s** of user writes. The WAL writes the data once, and compaction adds **write amplification of 10x** on top. Each disk sustains **1.5 GB/s** of writes.

What is the total physical write rate to disk (MB/s)?
steps: That is ~73% of one disk's 1.5 GB/s budget
assumptions: WA counted on top of WAL
drills.takeaway: Write amplification, not user traffic, decides SSD wear and disk throughput headroom.

drills.title: SSD endurance under write amplification
drills.prompt:
A node writes **50 MB/s** of user data; the LSM engine has **write amplification 12x** (including WAL). Its SSD is **4 TB** rated for **1 drive write per day (DWPD)**.

How many drive-writes per day does the workload consume?
steps: 13x the rating -> drive dies in weeks
drills.takeaway: Pick higher-endurance drives, spread writes over more drives, or tune compaction.

drills.title: Secondary index write amplification
drills.prompt:
A collection takes **20,000 inserts/s**. It has **6 secondary indexes** plus the `_id` index, and is in a **3-member replica set**.

How many index-entry writes per second happen across the replica set?
assumptions: Each index entry is one write
drills.takeaway: Every index taxes every write on every replica; audit indexes on write-heavy collections.

drills.title: Monthly compute cost
drills.prompt:
You need **120 VMs** at **$0.40/hour** each, running 24/7. Assume **730 hours/month**.

Monthly cost in dollars?
drills.takeaway: Reserved/savings plans (30-60% off) matter once a fleet is steady-state.

drills.title: Object storage cost for backups
drills.prompt:
You store **2 PB** of backups in blob storage. Hot tier is **$0.02/GB-month**, archive tier **$0.002/GB-month**. You move **90%** to archive.

New monthly storage cost in dollars?
drills.takeaway: Tiering cuts storage spend ~5x, but archive retrieval latency (hours) must fit your RTO.

drills.title: CDN egress cost
drills.prompt:
A video app serves **1 million hours of video/day** at **3 Mbps**. CDN egress costs **$0.01/GB**.

Monthly egress cost in dollars (30 days)?
steps: Per hour = 3 Mbps x 3,600 s / 8 = 1.35 GB
drills.takeaway: Egress is the dominant cost for media; bitrate ladders and codecs (AV1) are cost levers.

drills.title: LLM inference cost per day
drills.prompt:
A support assistant handles **2 million conversations/day**, each **4 turns**. Each turn sends **3,000 input tokens** and returns **300 output tokens**. Pricing: **$3 per 1M input**, **$15 per 1M output** tokens.

Daily cost in dollars?
drills.takeaway: Input context dominates; prompt caching or trimming history is the biggest saving.

drills.title: p99 latency budget across a call chain
drills.prompt:
A checkout API has an end-to-end **p99 SLO of 500 ms**. The path: edge + TLS **40 ms**, auth **20 ms**, fraud scoring **80 ms**, card network call **180 ms** (external). Remaining work is your ledger write.

What p99 budget (ms) remains for the ledger write, keeping a **20% safety margin** of the SLO?
drills.takeaway: An 80 ms p99 is tight for a replicated write; consider parallelise (fraud alongside auth) to buy slack.

drills.title: Fan-out tail latency
drills.prompt:
A search request fans out to **100 shards** in parallel and waits for all. Each shard independently exceeds **50 ms** with probability **1%** (its p99).

What percentage of user requests exceed 50 ms?
drills.takeaway: Shard p99 becomes user median at high fan-out; use hedged requests or partial results.

drills.title: Cross-region synchronous replication cost
drills.prompt:
A write must be **synchronously acknowledged** by a replica in another region (**RTT 70 ms**), plus **2 ms** local commit. A user operation performs **4 sequential writes**.

Minimum latency of the operation (ms)?
drills.takeaway: Batch writes into one transaction or go async cross-region; sequential geo-sync writes kill latency.

drills.title: Availability of serial dependencies
drills.prompt:
A request depends serially on **5 services**, each **99.9%** available.

What is the combined availability in percent?
drills.takeaway: Serial dependencies multiply unavailability; add caching, fallbacks or remove hops.
